verdict.root_cause: At 12:37:19, two minutes before onset, platform-automation set REDIS_ADDR on cartservice to redis-cart:6380, a non-default Redis port [tr_90a970cde810]. From then cartservice cannot finish initialization: it dials redis-cart:6380, times out, throws an unhandled exception from RedisCartStore.EnsureRedisConnected via Program.Main, and restarts every 30-50s without ever opening its gRPC listener [tr_fc5703a328a7]. With nothing listening on the cart port, checkoutservice's dial to 172.18.0.8:7070 is refused at TCP connect and surfaces at frontend as gRPC 13 INTERNAL wrapping a failed cart fetch plus bare 14 UNAVAILABLE [tr_cc66783452dd]. Checkout keeps accepting PlaceOrder requests that never reach completion lines [tr_2d543d3e7bcc]. The wrong port value is itself the mechanism: the address names an endpoint that refuses connection.
verdict.reasoning: The change log places a REDIS_ADDR port edit two minutes before onset and rules out the competing cartservice changes: the hotfix image was reverted ~30 min before onset and the latency-injecting container removed ~10 min before onset, so neither was in effect [tr_90a970cde810]. cartservice logs show exactly the consequence of that value — connect-stage failure to redis-cart:6380, an orderly application exception (not an OOM kill, not a request-path bug), and a restart loop preventing the gRPC server from listening [tr_fc5703a328a7]. Frontend's symptoms match a process that is not listening: received gRPC statuses with all frames in the grpc-js client path and an explicit refusal on a resolved IP:port at the conventional cart port [tr_cc66783452dd]. Frontend is not the origin — no changes recorded against it [tr_5e24b32a9fc1] and its error ratio fell rather than rose [tr_0239c6cc38bd]. Checkout is not the origin — it serves throughout with no post-12:40:30 downstream errors [tr_2d543d3e7bcc]. Not dependency_latency (refusal, not DEADLINE_EXCEEDED; injector gone before onset), not bad_deploy (pre-hotfix image at onset), not resource_exhaustion (orderly exception before each restart).
open_questions: No one checked the redis-cart service definition, so it is unconfirmed whether 6380 is wrong or whether redis-cart itself stopped listening — that would shift the fix to restarting redis-cart.
Frontend shows the same UNAVAILABLE signature at 12:09:51, ~28 minutes before the 12:37 edit [tr_cc66783452dd], unexplained by this cause alone.

Only 3 of 12 affected services were examined and 4 unmeasured edges were crossed; cartservice has no Prometheus series at all [tr_114d3aa288a4], so there is no metric confirmation of when cart traffic ceased.

alternatives.root_cause: redis-cart is itself down or not accepting connections, and cartservice's crash-loop is correct behaviour against a dead dependency.
alternatives.why_not: Never directly examined, so not excluded — but the change log independently records the port value being altered two minutes before onset [tr_90a970cde810], supplying a sufficient cause without positing an unobserved Redis outage.

alternatives.root_cause: The recurring automation cycle, not the specific value, is the fault: it repeatedly perturbs cartservice and any of its steps could destabilise the process.
alternatives.why_not: The other cycle steps were both reverted well before onset and the crash stack names the Redis connect specifically [tr_90a970cde810, tr_fc5703a328a7], so the mechanism is identified rather than diffuse.

proposal.expected_effect: Reverting cartservice's environment removes the REDIS_ADDR=redis-cart:6380 value set at 12:37:19 and recreates the container. In Loki, {service="cart-service"} should stop emitting the EnsureRedisConnected connect-timeout exception and the 30-50s restart cycle, and GetCartAsync/AddItemAsync request lines should resume. Downstream, frontend should stop logging gRPC 13 INTERNAL wrapping 'failed to get user cart' and 'dial tcp 172.18.0.8:7070 connection refused', and checkoutservice PlaceOrder lines should again be followed by payment-success and message-write lines. Note there is no Prometheus series for cartservice, so verification is by log lines and restart count only.
proposal.if_wrong: Falsified if cartservice still crash-loops on Redis connect after the revert, now naming the default port — that means 6380 was correct and redis-cart itself is not listening, shifting the fix to redis-cart. Also falsified if cartservice recovers but frontend keeps emitting the 14 UNAVAILABLE signature, which already appears at 12:09:51, ~28 minutes before the edit.
proposal.risk: If the diagnosis is inverted, this swaps in another unreachable address and adds a recreate to an already-restarting service, delaying the real fix. The revert restores the whole prior environment snapshot, not just REDIS_ADDR, so other bundled values move too. It does not stop the platform-automation cycle that has set and reverted this variable four times in ~21 hours, so the fault can return.
proposal.blast_radius: cartservice only. Its callers — frontend (cart reads) and checkoutservice (cart fetch during PlaceOrder) — see a brief connection reset during recreate, on top of an already-refused endpoint. redis-cart sees cart traffic return.

triage_judgement.reasoning: Critical multi-service alerting on frontend and checkoutservice within a minute, spanning the user-facing checkout path, is not dismissible. No open incident to attribute it to, and the alert pattern alone doesn't distinguish a shared downstream dependency from a deploy or resource issue.
